newsitem.title: USA: US targets nations for 97/8 subsidized wheat sales.
newsitem.headline: US targets nations for 97/8 subsidized wheat sales.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department on Monday targeted 75 nations for possible subsidized wheat sales in 1997/98 (July-June) under the Export Enhancement Program.

In a prepared statement announcing the action, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said USDA remains prepared to use export subsidies for wheat and other commodity exports "where needed and as appropriate."
But in actual fact, USDA has not subsidized wheat and other commodities under EEP for nearly two years.
USDA also targeted a large number of countries for subsidized sales of wheat flour, vegetable oil, barley, rice, frozen poultry, eggs and dairy goods in 1997/98.
The dairy products were offered under the Dairy Export Incentive Program, which USDA has used in the past two years to remain competitive in world markets.
Overall allocations for wheat and the other commodities are down from 1996-97, reflecting the US's committment to reduce export subsidies under the Uruguay Round trade pact, he said.
Favorable market conditions have enabled the U.S. to export wheat and other commodities in world markets without export subsidies for nearly two years.
USDA requested $500 million for EEP in fiscal 1998. But whether it will get that much remains highly uncertain.

Last week, the House appropriations subcommittee on agriculture approved just $270 million for EEP in fiscal 1998. But there are many steps left in the congressional process before a final EEP funding decision is made.
Further details of USDA's EEP and DEIP allocations follow:
